title: Void Ending in a Square to the Sun
source: Picatrix (adapted), Book I chapter 5, Book II chapter 3 and Book III chapter 1

<!-- generated by tools/content/gen-void.ts; edit the generator, not this file -->

The square is one of the two worst aspects in the lunar doctrine, an enmity the text grades as moderate because the signs it joins stand two natures apart. The counsel that guards every election runs exactly here: watch the square and the opposition in everything, and keep the Moon from the unfortunate planets in these figures above all.

When the Moon closes her course in a sign with a square to the Sun, the quiet stretch that follows carries something of his light and his generative heat. Picatrix calls the Sun the light of the world and the axis on which the universe turns; generative power flows from him, the heart is his seat in the body, gold is his metal, and the ruby and the jacinth his stones. His benevolence fits great royal achievements and kings. The whole lunar doctrine hangs on him, for in the text's accounting the stars and the Moon together sustain all vegetation and every composite body.
